## Rule
The input contains solid 3×3 monochrome blocks (here colors 8 and 7; other instance colors can vary). Extend each block as a 1-cell-wide horizontal and vertical line in the block's color, passing through the block's center row and center column, to the grid edges. The two arms cross through the 3×3 block. Where different-color extensions overlap/intersect, use the demonstrated conflict rule: the intersection is left unchanged/zero unless the original cell was nonzero, in which case preserve that original nonzero. In demo, color-8 horizontal line across row 5 (0-based) had a gap at column 13, where a color-7 vertical line crossed; color-7 horizontal line row 11 had gap at column 7 where color-8 vertical crossed. Original nonzero cells on extension paths are preserved, even when they differ from line color. Existing colored blocks remain intact.

## Evidence from demo
Demo input 17×18 had a 3×3 block of 8 at rows 4–6, cols 6–8, center row 5/col 7. It extended row 5 horizontally and col 7 vertically. Another 3×3 block of 7 at rows 10–12, cols 12–14, center row 11/col 13; it extended its center row and col. At crossing positions (r5,c13) and (r11,c7), the line colors conflicted and output was 0. Nonzero original markers along lines stayed as originally colored (e.g. input 7 at r15,c10 remains 7 on 8-extension; input 8 at r10,c6 remains 8 on 7-extension).

## This instance's solved output
19×19 grid, one-indexed block rows: 3–5 cols 7–9 were color 4; rows 8–10 cols 14–16 were color 8; rows 13–15 cols 1–3 were color 7. Centers: color4 r4,c8; color8 r9,c15; color7 r14,c2 (0-indexed). Extend each center row/column to boundaries, preserving original nonzero cells encountered; at conflicts between different extensions leave zero. The exact accepted output was the last assistant submission in the task transcript. Important correction: the color-7 vertical extension is column 1 (0-index), color-4 vertical is col 7, color-8 vertical is col 14; horizontal center rows are 13, 3, 8 respectively. At intersections r3,c14 (4 vs 8), r8,c7 (8 vs 4), r13,c7 (7 vs 4), r13,c14 (7 vs 8), conflict resolution as shown by accepted grid: preserve source nonzero at the location, otherwise zero.

## Operational lesson
Do not over-infer elaborate intersection behavior or overwrite original colored markers. Build output by copying input, drawing row/column rays from each block's center to the borders, and at each cell first preserve original nonzero; for blank cells fill only if exactly one color's ray passes through. If multiple distinct colors' rays collide in a blank cell, keep 0. Verify rows/columns and block centers systematically.
